Petitioner's case:
2.On December 2, 2015
, at about 12.45 hours, the petitioner was travelling in an Auto-rickshaw bearing Registration No.TN-02-AK-2588 as a passenger on Kamarajar Salai.

When the Auto-rickshaw turned onto Ramakrishna Mutt Salai,
Chennai, a Bus bearing Registration No.TN-01-N- 0625 belonging to the respondent / Corporation, approached from the opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner, and dashed against the Auto.
As a result, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over her body.
Hence, the respondent as the owner of the Bus is vicariously liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

2.1.Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was rushed to https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA NO.2 OF 2022 Government Hospital, Royapettah and thereafter referred to Rajiv Gandhi Government General Hospital.
The Doctor diagnosed that the petitioner suffered Fracture of Acctabulam Left, severe injury in the left thigh and multiple injuries all over the body.
She was discharged on January 1, 2016.
2.2.Subsequently, the petitioner was re-admitted in the same hospital on February 6, 2016, and discharged on February 22, 2016.
2.3.Then the petitioner was admitted in Neuro Life Hospital on March 30, 2016, where it was diagnosed that there was non-healing Ulcer over her left thigh and discharged on April 1, 2016.
2.4.According to the petitioner, she totally incurred a sum of Rs.45,593.93/- as medical expenses.
She was engaged in real estate business and thereby earned a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Therefore, the petitioner filed a claim petition before the Tribunal seeking compensation for a sum of Rs.15,00,000/-.

Respondent's case:
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA NO.2 OF 2022 3.The
respondent filed a counter wherein it has been stated that the accident occurred only due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Auto bearing Registration No.TN-02-AK-2588.
On seeing the negligent driving of the Auto driver, the Bus driver honked and slowed down allowing the Auto-rickshaw to overtake freely.
However, the Driver of the Auto tried to overtake on the left side of the Bus, lost control and caused the accident.
According to the respondent, the accident happened only due to the rash and negligent driving of the Driver of the Auto-rickshaw.
Accordingly, the respondent prayed to dismiss the Original Petition.
4.At trial, the petitioner was examined as P.W.1 and Dr.K.J.Mathiazhagan was examined as P.W.2 and Ex-P.1 to Ex-P.15 were marked on the side of the petitioner.

On the side of the respondent,
Mr.Karthikeyamani, Driver of the Bus was examined as R.W.1.

However, no documents were M.Kalaivani vs The Managing Director on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137557934/
2 marked on the side of the respondent.

sentences.text: Findings of the Tribunal https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA NO.2 OF 2022
5.Based on the evidence of P.W.1 and Ex-P.2 (First Information Report)
, the Tribunal came to the conclusion that the accident happened due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the respondent's Bus.
Though the petitioner averred that she was doing real estate business, as she did not produce any documents to substantiate her case, the Tribunal fixed notional income at Rs.9,000/- per month.
Further, the Tribunal concluded that the petitioner suffered 15% permanent disability which creates 15% functional disability.
Hence, the Tribunal applied multiplier method and awarded compensation of Rs.3,64,000/-.
6.Dissatisfied with the said Award, the appellant / petitioner has filed this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal.

Arguments:
7.The
learned counsel for the appellant / petitioner has submitted that the accident happened in the year 2015.

Due to the accident, the petitioner suffered Fracture of Acctabulam Left, severe injury in the left thigh and multiple injuries all over the body and she cannot perform her duty as she did b e f o r e t h e a c c i d e n t . T h e p e t i t i o n e r w a s a d m i t t e d i n H o s p i t a l f o r m o r e t h a n https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA NO.2 OF 2022 50 days.
Thereby, she underwent a lot of pain and sufferings.
7.1.She further submitted that the appellant / petitioner examined the Private Doctor (P.W.2), who examined her to prove her disability.
The Doctor had assessed her permanent disability at 40% and issued Disability Certificate to that effect, which is marked as Ex-P.15.
The Tribunal has not properly appreciated Ex-P.15  Disability Certificate issued by P.W.2 - Private Doctor and reduced the disability from 40 % to 15%.
Further that, vide its Order dated October 13, 2023, this Court directed the petitioner to appear before the Medical Board and obtain Disability Certificate.
Pursuant Disability Certificate shows that the petitioner suffers 15% permanent disability.
The fact that the petitioner suffers 15% permanent disability after about 8 years from the accident itself implies that the petitioner suffered greater permanent disability at the time of accident.
Hence, the evidence of P.W.2 - Private Doctor is reliable.
7.2.The Tribunal, without appreciating the facts and circumstances of the case in the right perspective, has awarded a meager compensation to the petitioner.
Accordingly, the learned Counsel prayed to https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA NO.2 OF 2022 allow the Civil Miscellaneous Appeal and enhance the compensation.

7.3. In support of her arguments, she would place reliance on the Judgement of the Honble Supreme Court in Erudhaya Priya Versus State Express Transport Corporation Ltd reported in 2020 SCC Online SC 601.

sentences.text: 8.Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent has submitted that the petitioner has not produced any document to prove her income.
However, the Tribunal has fixed a sum of Rs.9,000/- per month as notional income and rightly applied multiplier method and awarded compensation under the head 'future prospects' also.
Hence, there is no reason to interfere with the Award passed by the Tribunal.
Accordingly, learned counsel for the respondent prayed to dismiss the Civil Miscellaneous Appeal.
Discussion and Decision
9.This Court has considered the submissions made on either side and perused the materials available on record.

10.As far as negligence is concerned, the Tribunal, after https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA NO.2 OF 2022 considering the evidence of petitioner (P.W.1), the evidence of the respondent's Bus Driver (R.W.1) and Ex-P.2 (FIR) concluded that the accident had occurred only due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of respondent's Bus.
10.1.This Court has perused the evidence available on record.

Though the Counter Statement puts-forth a different version as to the manner of accident, R.W.1 in his cross examination has admitted that when he was turning the Bus right, left side of the Bus hit the Auto-rickshaw causing the accident.
10.2.Further, the appellant / petitioner has filed this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal seeking enhancement of compensation and the respondent has not filed any appeal / cross objection.
This Court has no reason to differ with the conclusion of the Tribunal.
Accordingly, this Court concurs with the Tribunal's findings.

Now, the only issues at hand are (i) permanent disability and (ii)
quantum of compensation.

11.As far as permanent disability is concerned, the Doctor (P.W.2) who examined the petitioner on August 1, 2019, has issued Ex.P-15 - Disability Certificate to the effect that the petitioner suffered 40% permanent https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA NO.2 OF 2022 disability.

Whereas, a Honble Division Bench this Court in Prabhus case [Tata AIG General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Prabhu and Others reported in (2016) 1 TN MAC 609], issued various directions with effect from August 1, 2016, with a view to maintain uniformity and certainty in medical assessment of permanent disability in Motor Accident Claims, and to weed out the issue of a select set of doctors,
who were stock witnesses, issuing liberal Disability Certificate in favour of the claimants.

entities.text: Tata AIG General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Prabhu and Others reported in (2016) 1 TN MAC 609
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Those include directions to the Tribunals to issue a letter to the Medical Board of the respective district, in the absence of it, to the nearest District Medical Board, to assess disability in Motor Accident Claims.
In the Original petition, Trial commenced on July 24, 2019.

In such a scenario, though P.W.2  Private Doctor examined the appellant / petitioner and issued Ex-P.15 (Disability Certificate), the Tribunal ought to have referred the petitioner to the Medical Board for obtaining Disability Certificate.
12.Be that as it may, this Court, vide its Order dated October 13, 2023, directed the petitioner to appear before the Medical Board and obtain Disability Certificate.

Accordingly, on February 2,
2024, the petitioner's disability was assessed by the Regional Medical Board, Government M.Kalaivani vs The Managing Director on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137557934/

sentences.text: The pursuant Disability Certificate was forwarded to this Court.
This Court is of the considered view that the Disability Certificate issued by the Medical Board is essential to arrive at a just compensation.

Accordingly, the Medical Certificate is hereby received and marked as Ex-C.1.
13.The

learned Counsel for the petitioner had contended that the petitioner enduring 15%
permanent disability about 8 years after the accident indicates that the petitioner experienced a greater permanent disability at the time of the accident.
Thus, she went on to argue that Ex-P.15 is reliable, and that compensation be decided based on Ex-P.15 i.e., by taking permanent disability at 40%.

14.Considering the Disability Certificates issued by the private doctor and the Medical Board, in view of Prabhus case (supra) as well as the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that Ex-C.1 - Disabilities Certificate issued by the Medical Board consisting of three expert doctors, should be given precedence.

Hence, this Court would decide the quantum of compensation based on Ex-C.1.
15.With regard to the quantum of compensation, the appellant / https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA NO.2 OF 2022 petitioner, aged 41 years at the time of accident, suffered fracture of Left Iliam,
Fracture of Acctabulam Left, fracture in her hip and multiple injuries all over the body.
She has taken treatment for more than 50 days.
Ex-C.1 shows that the petitioner suffers 15% permanent disability.

In regard of quantum of compensation, the learned Counsel for the petitioner would rely on Erudhaya Priyas case (supra) wherein the appellant was 23 years old, remained admitted in the hospital for eight months and suffered 31.1% permanent disability.
The compensation awarded therein was based on the facts and circumstances of that case, which is distinguishable from the instant case and hence, cannot be applied to the instant case.

16.Considering the nature of injuries, the permanent disability suffered by the petitioner as per Ex-C.1 and the hardships faced by the petitioner in performing her day-to-day chores/activities, this Court is of the view that the Tribunal has rightly applied multiplier method.
This Court does not find any fault / irregularity with the said approach of the Tribunal.

17.As far as monthly income is concerned, though the appellant / https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA NO.2 OF 2022 petitioner has stated that she was engaged in real estate business, she has not produced any documents to substantiate the same.
The accident occurred in the year 2015.
The Tribunal fixed notional income at Rs.9,000/- per month and arrived at a compensation of Rs.2,26,800/- towards functional disability.
This Court is of the view that the above sum is on the lower side.
17.1.Considering the age of the petitioner and the year of accident, this Court is of the view that the petitioner would have earned a sum of Rs.12,000/- per month.
Further, the petitioner is entitled to 25% future prospects as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi & Others [2017 (16) SCC 680].

5 18.The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings'.

sentences.text: Considering the nature of the injuries and the period of treatment undergone by the appellant / petitioner, a sum of Rs.20,000/- awarded under the head 'pain and sufferings' seems to be on the lower side.
Hence, this Court https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA NO.2 OF 2022 is inclined to enhance it to Rs.50,000/-.

19.The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards transportation; Rs.25,000/- under the head 'attender charges'; Rs.1,000/- under the head 'damages to clothes'; and Rs.45,593.93/- under the head 'medical expenses', which are, in the considered opinion of this Court, just and proper and hence, there is no warrant to interfere with the same.
20.The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.15,000/- under the head 'extra nourishment', which considering the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident, seems to be on the lower side.

Accordingly, this Court is inclined to enhance the same to Rs.25,000/-.
21.The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards 'loss of amenities' which also seems to be on the lower side.

Considering the nature of the injuries sustained, this Court is inclined to enhance the same to Rs.50,000/-
22.To sum up, this Court comes to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitled to get enhanced compensation of Rs.5,85,000/- (Rupees https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA NO.2 OF 2022 Five Lakh Eighty Five Thousand only) from the respondent in the following manner:

5 18.The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings'.

Considering the nature of the injuries and the period of treatment undergone by the appellant / petitioner, a sum of Rs.20,000/- awarded under the head 'pain and sufferings' seems to be on the lower side.
Hence, this Court https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA NO.2 OF 2022 is inclined to enhance it to Rs.50,000/-.

19.The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards transportation; Rs.25,000/- under the head 'attender charges'; Rs.1,000/- under the head 'damages to clothes'; and Rs.45,593.93/- under the head 'medical expenses', which are, in the considered opinion of this Court, just and proper and hence, there is no warrant to interfere with the same.
20.The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.15,000/- under the head 'extra nourishment', which considering the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident, seems to be on the lower side.

Accordingly, this Court is inclined to enhance the same to Rs.25,000/-.
21.The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards 'loss of amenities' which also seems to be on the lower side.

Considering the nature of the injuries sustained, this Court is inclined to enhance the same to Rs.50,000/-
